gas-mileage-calculator.quickAnswer: Enter the distance you drove and the fuel you used, and the tool computes your economy three ways: for example, 450 km on 32 litres is 14.1 km/L, or 7.1 L/100 km - about 33.1 MPG (US). Log every fill-up and the running average reveals your true long-term mileage.
keyFacts: Fuel economy = distance driven divided by fuel used. Same trip, three common expressions: km/L, L/100 km, MPG.
L/100 km is 'lower is better' (fuel per distance); km/L and MPG are 'higher is better' (distance per fuel).
Convert: MPG (US) = km/L x 2.352; L/100 km = 100 / (km/L).
Single fill-ups are noisy - brim the tank the same way each time and average over several fill-ups.
City driving, AC use, tyre pressure and speed all move the number more than most people expect.
howTo: Choose Metric (km / litres) or Imperial (miles / gallons).
Enter the distance driven since the last fill-up.
Enter the fuel used to refill the tank.
Press Add entry - the economy is computed and the entry joins your log.
Watch the running average across all entries for your true mileage.
gas-mileage-calculator.formula:
Economy = distance / fuel.
km/L = kilometres / litres.
L/100 km = 100 / (km/L).
MPG (US) = miles / gallons = (km/L) x 2.352.
Example: 450 km / 32 L = 14.06 km/L; 100 / 14.06 = 7.11 L/100 km; 14.06 x 2.352 = 33.1 MPG.
gas-mileage-calculator.workedExample:
You drove 450 km and refilled 32 litres.
1. km/L: 450 / 32 = 14.06 km/L.
2. L/100 km: 100 / 14.06 = 7.11 L/100 km.
3. MPG (US): 14.06 x 2.352 = 33.1 MPG.
4. Add a second entry: 520 km on 38 litres = 13.68 km/L.
5. Running average: (450 + 520) / (32 + 38) = 970 / 70 = 13.86 km/L.
benefits: Reveals your true mileage instead of the brochure figure.
A falling average is an early warning for tyre, engine or driving-habit issues.
Helps compare fuel costs between cars or routes with real numbers.
Your log never leaves the browser - no account needed.
limitations: Accuracy depends on consistent fill-ups; partial fills distort single entries (the average still converges).
Does not separate city vs highway driving unless you log them separately.
Fuel price and cost-per-km are not calculated - this is economy only.
MPG shown is US gallons; UK (imperial) gallons are larger - multiply by 1.201 for UK MPG.

faqs.q: Should I use km/L or L/100 km?
faqs.a: Both describe the same thing. India commonly uses km/L (higher is better); L/100 km (lower is better) is standard in Europe. The tool shows both.

faqs.q: How do I get accurate numbers?
faqs.a: Fill the tank to the same level each time, reset your trip meter, and average over at least 4-5 fill-ups. Single tanks are noisy.

faqs.q: What is the difference between US and UK MPG?
faqs.a: A US gallon is 3.785 litres; a UK gallon is 4.546 litres. UK MPG is about 1.2x the US figure. This tool reports US MPG.

faqs.q: Why did my mileage suddenly drop?
faqs.a: Common causes: low tyre pressure, clogged air filter, more city driving, AC use, or carrying extra weight. A persistent drop deserves a mechanic's look.

faqs.q: Can I log in miles and gallons?
faqs.a: Yes - switch to Imperial. Entries are converted internally, so you can even mix systems across entries.
Only in the page's memory while it is open. Closing the tab clears it - note down important numbers yourself.
